name: Jeong Seo 정서
bio: Jeong Seo (鄭敍) was a Goryeo court official of the twelfth century, known by the pen-name Gwajeong. Under King Uijong he was sent into exile at Dongnae, in the south-east, and the song that bears the name of his arbour there, Jeonggwajeong, is traditionally taken to be the lament he composed in banishment.

Jeonggwajeong is the only Goryeo gayo (court-and-folk song) in the Korean language whose author is known. In eleven short phrases the exiled speaker protests his innocence and pleads with the king to remember him. The song survives in the Akhak gwebeom (1493) and the Daeak hubo, and the date of its composition is still debated. The text here is the Middle Korean version on Korean Wikisource, without the musical section labels and modern-reading glosses.

poems.title: 정과정 (鄭瓜亭, Jeonggwajeong)
poems.author: Jeong Seo 정서
poems.text:
내 님믈 그리ᅀᆞ와 우니다니
山 졉동새 난 이슷ᄒᆞ요이다
아니시며 거츠르신 ᄃᆞᆯ 아으
殘月曉星이 아ᄅᆞ시리이다
넉시라도 님은 ᄒᆞᆫᄃᆡ 녀져라 아으
벼기더시니 뉘러시니잇가
過도 허믈도 千萬 업소이다
ᄆᆞᆯ힛마리신뎌
ᄉᆞᆯ읏븐뎌 아으
니미 나ᄅᆞᆯ 하마 니ᄌᆞ시니잇가
아소 님하 도람 드르샤 괴오쇼셔
